MARKE.|123 HOLY weeke.}}</noinclude>be. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=20}}† And vnles the Lord had shortened the daies, no flesh should be saued: but for the elect vvhich he hath elected, he hath {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Antichrists reigne shalbe three yeres and a halfe. ''Dan. 7. Apoc. 13''.}}∷ shortened the daies. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=21}}† And then if any man shal say vnto you, Loe, here is Christ: loe, there: do not beleeue. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=22}}† For there shal rise vp false-Christs and false-Prophets, and they shal shevv {{sup|‖}} signes and vvonders, to seduce (if it be possible) the elect also. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=23}}† You therfore take heede: behold I haue foretold you al things. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=24}}† But in those daies after that tribulation {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ez. 31, 7. Ioel. 3, 15.''}}* the sunne shal be darkened, and the moone shal not giue her light, {{verse|chapter=13|verse=25}}† and the starres of heauen shal be falling dovvne, and the povvers that are in heauen, shal be moued. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=26}}† And then they shal see the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Dan. 7, 13.''}}* Sonne of man comming in the cloudes, vvith much povver and glorie. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=27}}† And then shal he send his Angels, and shal gather together his elect from the foure vvindes, from the vttermost part of the earth to the vttermost part of heauen. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=28}}† And of the figtree learne ye a parable. VVhen novv the bough thereof is tender, and the leaues come forth, you knovv that sommer is very nigh. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=29}}† so you also vvhen you shal see these things come to passe, knovv ye that it is very nigh, at the doores. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=30}}† Amen I say to you, that this generation shal not passe, vntil al these things be done. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=31}}† Heauen and earth shal passe, but my vvordes shal not passe.

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=32}}† But of that day or houre no man knovveth, neither the Angels in heauen, nor the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Not as though him self knew not, as the Heretikes Agnoïtę held: but because he knew it not for to teach it others, as being not expedient. ''Ambr. de fide li. 5 c. 8''.}}∷ Sonne, but the Father. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=33}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel for a Cōfessor that is a Bishop, And on the Anniuersarie of the creation of a Bishop.}}Take heede, vvatch, and pray. for you knovv not vvhen the time is. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=34}}† Euen as a man vvho being gone into a strange countrie, left his house: and gaue his seruants authoritie * ouer ech vvorke, and commaunded the porter to vvatch. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=35}}† VVatch ye therfore (for you knovv not vvhen the lord of the house commeth: at euen, or at midnight, or at the cocke crovving, or in the morning) {{verse|chapter=13|verse=36}}† lest comming vpon a soden, he finde you sleeping. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=37}}† And that vvhich I say to you, I say to al, Vvatch.⊣

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. XIII.}}}}

''4. When shal these things be?''] The miseries which did fall before the destruction of the Temple and citie of Hierusalem, were a resemblance of the extreme calamitie that shal befall before the later day at the time of Antichrist: wherevpon Christ speaketh indifferently of both.

''6. I am he.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Arch-heretikes be False-Christs and False-Prophets.}}As before the destruction of Hierusalem, diuerse Seducers arose, and called them selues Christes, promising the people deliuerance from the feares and dangers they were in of<noinclude>{{rh||Q ij|forraine}}</noinclude>
